claim: In S. cerevisiae, the phosphate starvation (PHO) responsive transcription factors Pho4 and Pho2 are required for gene induction and survival during phosphate starvation.
source: In S. cerevisiae , the phosphate starvation (PHO) responsive transcription factors Pho4 and Pho2 are required for gene induction and survival during phosphate starvation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about S. cerevisiae and is supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: In C. glabrata, Pho4 is required but Pho2 is dispensable for survival in phosphate starvation.
source: In the related human commensal C. glabrata , Pho4 is required but Pho2 is dispensable for survival in phosphate starvation
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B demonstrating colony growth phenotypes.

claim: In C. glabrata, Pho2 is only partially required for inducing PHO genes.
source: In the related human commensal C. glabrata , Pho4 is required but Pho2 is dispensable for survival in phosphate starvation and is only partially required for inducing PHO genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1A showing phosphatase induction in pho2∆ strains.

claim: Reduced dependence on Pho2 evolved in C. glabrata and closely related species.
source: Phylogenetic survey suggests that reduced dependence on Pho2 evolved in C. glabrata and closely related species.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by phylogenetic survey data shown in Figure 2.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, less Pho2-dependent Pho4 orthologs induce more genes.
source: In S. cerevisiae , less Pho2-dependent Pho4 orthologs induce more genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3.

claim: In C. glabrata, Pho4 binds to more locations than Pho4 in S. cerevisiae does.
source: In C. glabrata , its Pho4 binds to more locations
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by ChIP-seq data showing 115 peaks for CgPho4 vs 74 peaks for ScPho4 in S. cerevisiae background (Figure 4A).

claim: In C. glabrata, Pho4 induces three times as many genes as Pho4 in S. cerevisiae does.
source: In C. glabrata , its Pho4 binds to more locations and induces three times as many genes as Pho4 in S. cerevisiae does.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing ~70 target genes in C. glabrata vs ~20 in S. cerevisiae.

claim: Evolution of combinatorial regulation allows for rapid expansion of a gene regulatory network's targets.
source: Our work shows how evolution of combinatorial regulation allows for rapid expansion of a gene regulatory network's targets, possibly extending its physiological functions.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the experimental findings throughout the manuscript.

claim: Combinatorial regulation is a common feature in gene regulatory networks.
source: Although combinatorial regulation is a common feature in gene regulatory networks, how it evolves and affects network structure and function is not well understood.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: S. cerevisiae and C. glabrata share ~90% of their gene repertoire.

evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Gabaldón et al., 2013.

claim: S. cerevisiae and C. glabrata have an average of ~67% protein sequence identity.
source: share ~90% of their gene repertoire and have an average of ~67% protein sequence identity (Gabaldón et al., 2013)

claim: In phosphate replete conditions, Pho4 is phosphorylated and localized to the cytoplasm in S. cerevisiae.

claim: As extracellular inorganic phosphate concentration drops, dephosphorylated Pho4 is imported into the nucleus in S. cerevisiae.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, Pho4 functions together with Pho2 to activate PHO gene expression.

claim: Pho4 regulates fewer than 30 genes in S. cerevisiae.

claim: Both transcriptional and binding assays are consistent with the hypothesis that CgPho4 evolved to be stronger in DNA-binding and in inducing gene expression.
source: While the mechanism for this reduction in co-activator dependence is not clear, both transcriptional and binding assays are consistent with the hypothesis that CgPho4 evolved to be stronger in DNA-binding and in inducing gene expression (Figure 4)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a hypothesis consistent with experimental data.

claim: A significant change in the size of the regulon was observed (~20 target genes in S. cerevisiae vs.~70 in C. glabrata).
source: Unlike previous studies which found conserved network output despite regulatory rewiring (Tsong et al., 2006; Kuo et al., 2010; Habib et al., 2012), we observed a significant change in the size of the regulon (~20 target genes in S. cerevisiae vs.~70 in C. glabrata)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: The organization of a stress response GRN may allow it to be more evolutionarily plastic in acquiring and shedding targets as the environment shifts.
source: The organization of a stress response GRN may allow it to be more evolutionarily plastic in acquiring and shedding targets as the environment shifts, creating new demands while eliminating old ones.
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the discussion based on the observed differences.

claim: Expression divergence evolves more readily among stress responsive genes compared to growth control and general metabolism genes.
source: Consistent with this view, previous studies showed that expression divergence evolves more readily among stress responsive genes compared to growth control and general metabolism genes (Thompson and Regev, 2009)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation.

claim: Trans evolution in CgPho4 altered its dependence on the co-activator and resulted in a dramatic expansion in its targets.
source: However, we find that trans evolution in CgPho4, which conserved the core DNA binding specificity and thus the existing targets, altered its dependence on the co-activator, and resulted in a dramatic expansion in its targets.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Compared to target turnover via cis regulatory changes, the trans evolutionary mechanism is likely much more rapid.
source: Compared to target turnover via cis regulatory changes, this trans evolutionary mechanism is likely much more rapid, and may allow natural selection to quickly sample many potential targets at once.
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the discussion.

claim: The reduction in Pho2-dependence likely evolved gradually.
source: However, it should be noted that the reduction in Pho2-dependence likely evolved gradually (Figures 2B and 3C)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on data shown in Figures 2B and 3C.

claim: Evolution of combinatorial regulation can lead to rapid rewiring of a gene regulatory network.
source: In conclusion, we demonstrated that evolution of combinatorial regulation can lead to rapid rewiring of a gene regulatory network.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion based on the findings.

claim: Changes affecting the interaction between transcription factors and their cofactors may be an important yet underappreciated mechanism underlying gene regulatory network evolution.
source: More generally, changes affecting the interaction between transcription factors and their cofactors may be an important yet underappreciated mechanism underlying gene regulatory network evolution (Slattery et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated as a general conclusion in the discussion with a citation.

claim: Only 16 of the 79 genes directly induced by CgPho4 in C. glabrata are involved in maintaining phosphate homeostasis.
source: Only 16 of the 79 genes directly induced by CgPho4 in C. glabrata are involved in maintaining phosphate homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on GO analysis.

claim: A significant number (25 genes) of CgPho4 targets are predicted to be involved in responses to non-phosphate related stresses.
source: Among the remaining genes, a significant number (25 genes) are predicted to be involved in the response to non-phosphate-related stresses, including osmotic (seven genes) and oxidative (seven genes) stresses.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on GO analysis.

claim: A smaller group of CgPho4 targets (9 and 3 genes) have potential functions in cell wall synthesis and cell adhesion.
source: In addition to roles in other stress responses, a smaller group of CgPho4 targets (9 and 3 genes) have potential functions in cell wall synthesis and cell adhesion
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on GO analysis.

claim: Cell wall synthesis and cell adhesion are traits known to be relevant for survival and virulence in the host.
source: two traits that were known to be relevant for survival and virulence in the host (Atanasova et al., 2013; De Las Peñas et al., 2015; Luo and Samaranayake, 2002; Jawhara et al., 2012; Fabre et al., 2014)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations.

claim: Pho4 in C. albicans has been shown to be important for survival under particular types of osmotic and oxidative stresses.
source: Intriguingly, Pho4 in C. albicans has been shown to be important for survival under particular types of osmotic and oxidative stresses, suggesting a similar functional expansion as we observed in C. glabrata (Ikeh et al., 2016)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation.

claim: In C. albicans, phosphate starvation was linked to enhanced virulence.
source: Also in C. albicans, phosphate starvation was linked to enhanced virulence
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation.

claim: A strain lacking Pho4 in C. albicans displayed extensive filamentation in response to phosphate limitation.
source: and a strain lacking Pho4 displayed extensive filamentation in response to phosphate limitation (Romanowski et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation.

claim: Stress responses in commensal species may have evolved to be more coordinated.
source: Combining these observations, we speculate that stress responses in the commensal species may have evolved to be more coordinated
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the discussion.

claim: Stress responses in commensal species may have acquired new targets linked to virulence.
source: and may have acquired new targets linked to virulence, to cope with the distinct stress profiles in the host
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the discussion.
